title: observability-live-observation.v1
description: What was READ BACK from a running control plane, as one document. AGENTS.md rule 12 names three independently comparable artifacts: the desired state (this repository at a commit, rendered to a known tree digest), the last verified receipt (`promotion-receipt.schema.json`), and live state. The first two were contracts and the third was a habit of reading APIs in the right order, which is not an artifact and cannot be compared later, attached to a ticket or replayed against a different desired state. This is the third one.  Every field is a count, a boolean, a digest, an enum, a logical name or a timestamp — the same discipline the receipt keeps, and for the same reason. There is deliberately NO field an endpoint, a port, a scrape URL, a credential basename or an error string can be typed into: `last_error` would carry the target's address in most real failures, so target failure is reported as a health enum and the address is established from the private inventory whose digest the receipt already carries (ADR-0004, rule 18). The document is therefore safe to attach to a ticket, which is what makes it usable as evidence.  It is PRODUCED by the promotion facility — the thing that can reach the host — and CONSUMED by `live_verify.py`, which performs no I/O. That split is why the six production conditions can be unit-tested without a running stack.

host_target_id.description: The LOGICAL host, spelled as the receipt spells it. Its resolved identity is in the private inventory.

previous.description: The pointer captured BEFORE activation. Null only on the very first promotion; any later null means the rollback target was not captured (rule 11).

tree.description: Every file the read-back found under the active release, by path and digest. COMPLETE, never sampled: an entry absent here is compared as missing, and a path present here that the render does not produce is compared as unexpected — a stale file left in the release directory is still mounted into the evaluator. An empty array is refused by the verifier rather than passing as 'nothing differs', because a read-back that failed to list anything reports exactly as a clean one does.

targets.description: One entry per ACTIVE target, not per job: a job resolving to four endpoints contributes four entries, which is what makes the declared `expected` count checkable.

rules.description: Every rule LOADED by the evaluator, with its evaluation health. AGENTS.md rule 10: absence is not health, so a rule the desired state declares and this array omits is a finding rather than a silence.

routes.description: The resolved route tree, by declared route id and the receiver it lands on.

probes.description: One entry per declared surface PER ADDRESS FAMILY. A `dual_stack` surface with one entry is an incomplete pass, never a passing one: IPv4 and IPv6 traverse different chains on this host and a v4-only probe has repeatedly passed over a live v6 exposure.

path.description: Relative to the release root, spelled as the renderer spells it.

tree_entry.description: A digest rather than the bytes. The rendered tree legitimately contains resolved endpoints and credential basenames; its digest does not, and a digest is all a comparison needs.

health.description: Prometheus's own vocabulary. There is deliberately no `last_error`: the address of the target it could not reach is in almost every such message, and one field carrying it would undo rule 18 for the whole document.

counter.description: The ingestion counter this observation read, named so a comparison against a baseline of a DIFFERENT counter is a refusal rather than an accidental pass.

value.description: The absolute counter value. The verifier asserts a DELTA against a recorded baseline, never that this is zero: `counter == 0` is satisfiable by a reset, a fresh TSDB or a container restart, and a predicate made true that way cannot be told from one made true by a repair (rule 30).

process_start_time.description: `process_start_time_seconds` from the same evaluator, in the same read. This is what makes the reset undetectable-by-omission impossible: a counter that went backwards is caught by comparing values, and a counter that was reset and climbed back past the baseline is caught only by noticing the process restarted underneath it.

delivered.description: Proved AT THE RECEIVER. A 200 from a delivery API is Alertmanager's outbound attempt succeeding, which is not evidence a human can be reached.

receiver_evidence_ref.description: Where at the receiver the delivery was seen — a message id, a thread reference, a log coordinate. The verifier refuses `delivered: true` without one, because a boolean with nothing behind it is the claim, not the proof.

chain.description: The chain the rule for this surface was OBSERVED in. Compared against the chain the surface's kind and family derive (rule 23): seven IPv6 DROP rules were found on this host in `DOCKER-USER`, which no IPv6 packet to a published port traverses, so every port they named read as closed and was open.

expectation.description: What the declared exposure says should happen, derived from the desired state rather than typed by the prober.

outcome.description: A control that is expected to SUCCEED, run in the same pass on the same address family. Without it a refusal proves the probe ran, not that access is shut: an unplugged cable, a wrong address family or a dead prober all present as `refused`.

positive_control.description: Structurally nested inside the probe, and deliberately not a sibling array. A control listed alongside the probes could be matched to the wrong family by a later reader; nested, an IPv6 probe cannot borrow an IPv4 control.

restored_digest.description: The tree digest read back AFTER the restore. Compared against the digest the previous release was accepted with: a rollback that restored a pointer without restoring the bytes is the failure this field exists to catch.

rollback.description: Absent when no rollback was attempted in this pass. The verifier treats absence as condition 6 unproven rather than passed — a rollback that has never been exercised is a plan, not a capability.
